title: System Voltage Malfunction (P0560-v4)
shortDescription: A system voltage / charging fault (Malfunction) stored as P0560-v4.
fullDescription: The control module logs P0560-v4 when the monitored system voltage shows a malfunction condition for longer than the calibrated time window. The PCM may disable non-essential loads, illuminate the battery / charging warning, and limit auto-stop or accessory features. The fault may persist until the underlying circuit or component is repaired and the code cleared with a scan tool.
safetyImpact: A failing charging system can leave the vehicle unable to restart; tow if the warning lamp is red.

causes.cause: Loose or corroded battery cables / grounds

fixSteps.title: Battery Test
fixSteps.instruction: Perform a conductance test on the battery; replace if SOH below 70%.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cables & Grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the battery posts and tighten the engine / chassis ground straps.

fixSteps.title: Charging System Test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify alternator output of 13.5-14.7 V at 2000 RPM with light load and full load.

fixSteps.title: Replace Alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Replace alternator if regulation is out of spec or LIN data is missing.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short trips only — if the alternator fails the engine will stall when the battery drains.

faq.q: Will a new battery clear it?
faq.a: Sometimes; if the alternator or wiring is the root cause the code returns within a drive cycle.

title: Auto Stop / Start General (P05A0)
shortDescription: An auto stop-start system fault (General) stored as P05A0.
fullDescription: The control module logs P05A0 when the auto stop-start strategy detects a general condition that prevents safe engine restart. The PCM disables auto-stop, illuminates the stop-start warning, and may also block remote start until the fault is corrected. The fault may persist until the underlying circuit or component is repaired and the code cleared with a scan tool.
safetyImpact: Auto-stop is disabled; the vehicle remains drivable but fuel economy will drop.

causes.cause: Hood / brake / seat-belt switch logic fault

symptoms: Auto stop-start indicator amber or off
HVAC blower drops during stop event

fixSteps.title: Test Auxiliary Battery
fixSteps.instruction: Load test the AGM or auxiliary 12 V battery and replace if marginal.

fixSteps.title: Check IBS Calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool to view battery state of charge and SOH; relearn after replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Tandem Starter
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for delayed engagement; replace the enhanced starter assembly if worn.

fixSteps.title: Update Software
fixSteps.instruction: Apply OEM TSB software updates that refine stop-start logic.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving?
faq.a: Yes — auto-stop simply stays disabled; the engine runs normally.

faq.q: Will a normal flooded battery work?
faq.a: No — stop-start systems require AGM or EFB chemistry to handle the cycling load.

title: Hybrid / 12V Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit (P0AAB-v3)
shortDescription: A battery temperature sensor / pack thermal fault (Sensor A Circuit) stored as P0AAB-v3.
fullDescription: The control module logs P0AAB-v3 when the battery management module sees a sensor a circuit reading from a battery temperature sensor. Charging current is limited, regenerative braking may reduce, and stop-start can be disabled until temperatures normalize. The fault may persist until the underlying circuit or component is repaired and the code cleared with a scan tool.
safetyImpact: Severe over-temperature events should be treated as urgent — pull over if you smell hot electrolyte.

causes.cause: Battery cooling fan blocked or failed
Sensor harness shorted to ground or open

symptoms: Reduced power / limp message after long drives
Hybrid battery fan running at high speed
Electric range reduced on plug-in models
Charging stops early on AC charge

fixSteps.title: Read Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare individual battery temp sensor readings; outliers indicate a failed NTC.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cooling Path
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the battery cooling intake (often under rear seat) and verify fan operation.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm the NTC at known ambient and compare to the OEM resistance table.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor / Module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed sensor or BMS submodule and clear adaptations.

faq.q: Can I drive normally?
faq.a: Yes if the warning is amber; pull over immediately for any red battery icon.

faq.q: Does cabin AC affect this?
faq.a: On many hybrids cabin air cools the battery; keep AC running in hot weather.

Sensor harness shorted to ground or open

symptoms: Reduced power / limp message after long drives
Hybrid battery fan running at high speed
Electric range reduced on plug-in models
Charging stops early on AC charge

fixSteps.title: Read Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare individual battery temp sensor readings; outliers indicate a failed NTC.

fixSteps.instruction: Clean the battery cooling intake (often under rear seat) and verify fan operation.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm the NTC at known ambient and compare to the OEM resistance table.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor / Module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed sensor or BMS submodule and clear adaptations.

title: Belt Alternator Starter (BAS) Hybrid Battery Charge State (P0EE0-v3)
shortDescription: A BAS / mild-hybrid 48 V / motor-generator fault (Hybrid Battery Charge State) stored as P0EE0-v3.
fullDescription: The control module logs P0EE0-v3 when the hybrid control module reports a hybrid battery charge state condition from the belt alternator-starter. Mild-hybrid boost and regenerative recovery are disabled; the vehicle reverts to conventional starter operation. The fault may persist until the underlying circuit or component is repaired and the code cleared with a scan tool.
safetyImpact: Vehicle remains drivable; loss of torque-fill may be noticed during launch.

causes.cause: BAS belt slipping or worn tensioner

fixSteps.title: Inspect BAS Belt
fixSteps.instruction: Check the BAS belt for cracks and verify tensioner spring force.

fixSteps.title: Scan HV Status
fixSteps.instruction: Read 48 V battery state of charge and interlock status; look for paired U-codes.

fixSteps.title: Test DC-DC Converter
fixSteps.instruction: Verify converter output is regulated to 14 V under load.

fixSteps.title: Replace BAS Unit
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the belt alternator-starter and program with HV credentials.

faq.q: Is the 48 V system dangerous?
faq.a: It is below the 60 V touch-safe threshold, but follow OEM HV procedures and use insulated tools.

faq.q: Will a normal mechanic fix this?
faq.a: Most independent shops can; replacement BAS belts require special tensioner tools.

title: PCM / Sensor Reference Intake Air Heater Control (P0640)
shortDescription: A PCM internal control / sensor reference fault (Intake Air Heater Control) stored as P0640.
fullDescription: The control module logs P0640 when the powertrain module's self-test detects a intake air heater control condition on its internal control or sensor reference circuit. Multiple sensors may report implausible data, the MIL is illuminated, and the engine may enter limp-home. The fault may persist until the underlying circuit or component is repaired and the code cleared with a scan tool.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and unstable idle are common; fix promptly before downstream damage occurs.

causes.cause: Shorted 5 V reference (sensor pulling rail down)
Failed PCM main relay or power feed

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
Sudden loss of communication with scan tool
Cooling fans running with key off

fixSteps.title: Check Power & Grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all PCM B+, ignition, and ground circuits are within spec.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect Sensors One-by-One
fixSteps.instruction: If a 5 V reference is pulled low, isolate the offending sensor by sequential disconnection.

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCM Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Look for water intrusion, green corrosion, and pushed-back terminals.

fixSteps.title: Reflash or Replace PCM
fixSteps.instruction: Apply the latest calibration; replace and program if internal failure is confirmed.

faq.q: Do I need to replace the PCM?
faq.a: Only after ruling out shorted sensors and bad grounds; many shops swap unnecessarily.

faq.q: Will a used PCM work?
faq.a: It must be VIN-programmed — used modules typically need security relearn at a dealer.
